newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's VSM plans 240 bln rbl bond issue Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: Russia's VSM plans 240 bln rbl bond issue Oct 3.

text.p: RAO Vysokoskorostnye Magistrali (VSM or High-Speed Railways) plans to make a second 240 billion rouble one-year government-backed bond issue on October 3, a company official said on Tuesday.

VSM will send the prospectus to the finance ministry for official approval on Thursday, but the date, volume and other details have been agreed in principle with the ministry, deputy finance director Andrei Nikandrov told Reuters.
"The bonds will allow us to carry on with work before other (financial) sources which are being negotiated now," he said. "These are tied government credits from Britain, and other sources."
The company is raising funds to build a high-speed Moscow-St Petersburg rail link.
Russia recently approved a $200 million British loan for constructing the St Petersburg terminus by U.K. construction company Taylor Woodrow Plc.
Nikandrov said he expected to get the finance ministry's approval for the new bond issue on Monday or Tuesday.
VSM issued 120 billion roubles of government-backed bonds on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange at the beginning of the year.
The securities are effectively the same as Russian OFZ interest-bearing government bonds. OFZ bonds pay quarterly interest linked to current issues of GKO discount Treasury bills.
